headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading action paths exist because aci has broad egress and MCP/function-calling access while Chatwoot handles customer data and integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or an MCP server, and Chatwoot exposes integration surfaces like Slack and Linear. If Chatwoot content is routed into aci through a shared workspace or message bridge, attacker-controlled text could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot messages or tickets are forwarded into aci via MCP, Slack, or files without provenance tags
IF aci parses imported content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any automatic forwarding from Chatwoot to aci
Add a strict instruction/data separator in the bridge
Require human review before aci acts on imported text
Use allowlisted command schemas only
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking across the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci has broad network egress and handles email, CRM, calendar, and secrets management, while Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, and interaction history. If either agent shares a workspace or passes customer records into aci, aci can exfiltrate them to third-party services by default. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF customer records from Chatwoot are placed into aci's context or workspace
IF aci is allowed to call external APIs while holding those records
mitigations: Remove sensitive fields before transfer
Restrict aci egress to approved domains
Keep Chatwoot and aci on separate workspaces
Rotate any shared secrets immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and multiple external integrations, and aci explicitly supports multiple instances. If they operate on the same CRM, email, or support records, concurrent writes can race and overwrite each other. Chatwoot is not shown to have locking, so conflict risk exists in default multi-agent deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM, email, or support queue
IF no external lock or optimistic concurrency control is configured
mitigations: Assign one system as the write owner
Serialize writes through a queue
Enable record version checks
Limit overlapping integrations
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate actions through APIs and MCP, while Chatwoot exposes support workflows and integrations that may consume upstream outputs. If Chatwoot treats aci-produced summaries or recommendations as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect customer responses or ticket actions. The pathway is plausible, but the profiles do not prove automatic trust by default.
conditions: IF Chatwoot workflows ingest aci outputs without verification
IF aci is allowed to trigger downstream support actions or drafts
mitigations: Require approval before sending customer-facing replies
Show source citations beside aci outputs
Add a verification step in Chatwoot workflows
Disable auto-send on generated content
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data, while Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, and interaction history. If EU or regulated customer data flows between them, differing retention or residency policies could create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is shared between the two systems
IF their retention or residency policies differ for that data class
mitigations: Map data classes to each system
Block regulated fields from cross-system sync
Document retention settings for both tools
Review vendor DPAs before enabling sync
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
